34032889.correction: world z -0.015 m vs `pose_uncalibrated_solve`, applied by hand. History, each step a response to observed grasp height on this rig: -0.010 on 2026-09-10 (grasps ~1cm high); -0.010 more on 2026-09-15, total -0.020 (runs through the first correction were still ~1cm high); +0.005 on 2026-09-15, total -0.015 (at -0.020 grasps came in ~0.5cm LOW). The last two steps bracket the answer: the residual is now sub-centimetre and the true offset sits between -0.010 and -0.020, near -0.015. Note the bracket is not self-consistent for a pure constant -- 1cm high at -0.010 implies -0.020, 0.5cm low at -0.020 implies -0.015 -- so these are eyeball estimates, and -0.015 is the midpoint that satisfies both to within their precision.
34032889.source: copied from droid 34032889_left in /home/prpl/tamp-vla/droid/droid/calibration/calibration_info.json (the robot env's editable `droid` points at the tamp-vla checkout, not ~/droid -- ~/droid's copy is stale at 2026-08-12), recalibrated 2026-09-10 22:52, THEN HAND-CORRECTED -- see `correction` for the step-by-step history. `pose` is NOT the raw solve. Since load_calibration() applies translation in the world frame, the bias shifts every point reconstructed through this camera down 1.5cm in world z regardless of the camera's tilt, which moves grasps and placements alike. CAVEATS: (a) the fudge only moves perception that comes through THIS serial -- the wrist cam (13222437) and any top cam still carry the original bias, so if the true cause is the TCP/gripper offset rather than these extrinsics, it is only masked for the side view. cameras.perception is a SERVER-owned setting (data-collection's top-bar selector -> TIPTOP_PERCEPTION_CAMERA); flipping it to `hand` exposes the full uncorrected bias. (b) tiptop's update_calibration_info() rewrites an entry as {pose, timestamp} only, so the next `calibrate-third-person-cam` run on this serial silently discards this correction AND these notes -- re-apply the -0.015 m by hand after any recalibration, or the error comes back. (c) a settled ~1.5cm constant z offset is well OUTSIDE this camera's run-to-run solve scatter (consecutive solves agreed to 6.6mm / 0.47deg), so the extrinsics are unlikely to be the true cause: a genuine 1.5cm z error would have shown up as disagreement between solves and did not. Treat this as a standing correction to be retired once the TCP/gripper offset is measured directly. Prior solve history: 2026-09-10 22:52 superseded 2026-09-10 22:16 by 6.6mm / 0.47deg, which superseded 2026-09-04 18:06 by 6.1mm / 0.63deg; both inside the ~10-15mm / <1deg run-to-run scatter of the 08-26..08-27 cluster, so those read as repeat solves of one mount position. world_from_cam, the left ZED frame -- which is the frame tiptop's rgb/K_left come from. NOTE: only read when DC_WORKSPACE=prpl; a bare run falls back to assets/calibration_info.json
